title: Allow passing a user name to the gitcreds lookup in gh_token()
description:
`gh_token()` resolves the token with `gitcreds::gitcreds_get(host_url)`, where `host_url` is the bare host (e.g. `https://github.com`). gitcreds can select between several credentials for a host by putting the user name in the URL, but gh has no convenient way to pass one through. So with more than one credential for the host the helper returns whichever it enumerates first.

### Reprex(ish)

Two github.com credentials in the macOS keychain, one written by `gitcreds::gitcreds_set()` (default user name `PersonalAccessToken`, a classic PAT with `admin:org`) and one written back by git after an HTTPS operation through the GitHub CLI's helper (user name `x-access-token`, a `gho_` token with `gist, repo, workflow`).

```r
gitcreds::gitcreds_get("https://PersonalAccessToken@github.com")$username
#> [1] "PersonalAccessToken"
gitcreds::gitcreds_get("https://x-access-token@github.com")$username
#> [1] "x-access-token"

# gh only ever asks for the bare host, so the choice is up to the helper
gitcreds::gitcreds_get("https://github.com")$username
#> [1] "x-access-token"
gh::gh_whoami()$scopes
#> [1] "gist, repo, workflow"
```

This recently bit me when an entry came back flipped during a single afternoon after git rewrote both keychain items. Previously running code started failing with scope errors even though the intended PAT was still stored.

### Solutions

Would you consider a way to pass a user name into the gitcreds lookup? I'm not sure what the best entry point for that information would be - function argument, package option, env variable, etc.

It also looks like just adding an account into `GITHUB_API_URL` will potential cause issues since some functions make assumptions about the url pattern.

My current work around is `git config --global credential.https://github.com.username PersonalAccessToken`, but that changes behavior for most git operation to the host, not just gh.

### Versions

gh 1.6.1.9000, gitcreds 0.1.2, macOS, Apple Git 2.54 with the `osxkeychain` helper.

title: Authenticated GET cache is not isolated by token
description:
gh() caches GET responses by URL without distinguishing authentication tokens. This causes token-dependent GET responses to be reused after the caller switches tokens, potentially returning data associated with the previous token.

```r
valid_token <- gh::gh_token()
invalid_token <- paste0("ghp_", strrep("x", 36))

first <- gh::gh("/user", .token = valid_token)
second <- gh::gh("/user", .token = invalid_token)

identical(first$login, second$login)
#> [1] TRUE

# Disabling the cache produces the expected authentication error.
options(gh_cache = FALSE)
gh::gh("/user", .token = invalid_token)
#> Error: GitHub API error (401): Bad credentials
```

Expected behavior: authenticated responses should never be reused across tokens. GitHub responses use Vary: Authorization, so the cache should account for that header, partition entries by authentication context, or avoid caching authenticated requests.

Observed with gh 1.6.1.

If this makes more sense as an upstream issue with httr2 I'm happy to move it there.

title: Length of ghs tokens increasing
description:
GitHub has [started to roll out app tokens that are longer](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-04-24-notice-about-upcoming-new-format-for-github-app-installation-tokens/) and break the `validate_gh_pat()` check.

https://github.com/r-lib/gh/blob/e9194ae1bb2993ba8f72d9da2f07679b5e3e013a/R/gh_token.R#L93-L116

They say "The overall length of the tokens will be longer (~520 characters) and will vary based on the data stored within it." The "~" there is annoying, so I'm not sure EXACTLY what should be allowed, but something along these lines should work:

```r
  if (
    x == "" ||
      # https://github.blog/changelog/2021-03-04-authentication-token-format-updates/
      # Fine grained tokens start with "github_pat_".
      # https://github.blog/changelog/2022-10-18-introducing-fine-grained-personal-access-tokens/
      grepl(
        "^(gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9_]{36,251}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{36,244}|ghs_[A-Za-z0-9_]+)$",
        x
      ) ||
      grepl("^[[:xdigit:]]{40}$", x)
  ) {
    x
  } else {
    url <- "https://gh.r-lib.org/articles/managing-personal-access-tokens.html"
    cli::cli_abort(c(
      "Invalid GitHub PAT format",
      "i" = "A GitHub PAT must have one of four forms:",
      "*" = "40 hexadecimal digits (older PATs)",
      "*" = "A 'ghp_' prefix followed by 36 to 251 more characters (newer PATs)",
      "*" = "A `ghs_` prefix followed by about 500 characters (GitHub App installation tokens)",
      "*" = "A 'github_pat_' prefix followed by 36 to 244 more characters (fine-grained PATs)",
      "i" = "Read more at {.url {url}}."
    ))
  }
}
```

I'm seeing sporadic failures on GitHub Actions that look like they are caused by this.

I'll submit a PR shortly.

raw_pr_dat <- raw_prs %>%
  # strip the gh_response class to make tidyr happy about unnesting

title: Unable to use `gh::gh()` with public repositories on GitHub if SAML turned on (GitHub Enterprise) if a PAT has been created
description:
## Background
We have public repositories on GitHub Enterprise. SAML is turned on. But the repos are fully public and there are no restrictions to downloading, cloning, or forking. But if we try to use gh::gh() with those repositories, we get an error if the user has a PAT. Deleting the PAT will cause the installation to work, however, there may be instances where people do not want to delete the PAT because they are using it for other things. The error is only with public repos on GitHub Enterprise with SAML turned on. See [a similar issue with the `remotes` package](https://github.com/r-lib/remotes/issues/818) that other people in our GitHub Enterprise just posted.

## How to Reproduce
** this was reproduced using posit cloud***

1. Make sure a PAT is created.
```
usethis::create_github_token() 
credentials::set_github_pat("YourPAT")
```
2. Try to use {gh} to get the latest release from a repository on GitHub Enterprise where SAML is turned on. The following error appears:
```
gh::gh("GET /repos/nmfs-ost/ss3-source-code/releases/latest", page = 1)
Error in `gh::gh()`:
! GitHub API error (403): Resource protected by
  organization SAML enforcement. You must grant your Personal
  Access token access to this organization.
ℹ Read more at
  <https://docs.github.com/articles/authenticating-to-a-github-organization-with-saml-single-sign-on/>
Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.
```

* adding the .token = NULL parameter created the same error

3. Delete the PAT
```
usethis::edit_r_environ()
gitcreds::gitcreds_delete()
```
4.  Restart R and try gh again
```
gh::gh("GET /repos/nmfs-ost/ss3-source-code/releases/latest", page = 1)
```

## Possible solution

Create a parameter that tells the function to not look for a token, such as `dont_use_token = TRUE` that would not use gh_token().

By commenting out lines, adding the modified lines in the package, and trying the reloaded gh package with my modifications using a PAT again resolved the issue for me. Of course you wouldn't want to do exactly as I did because in many situations you want the token, but having an option to use my replacement with something like what I suggested above would be helpful.

In gh_request.R
```
# auth <- gh_auth(x$token %||% gh_token(x$api_url))
auth <- gh_auth(x$token)
```

In gh_rate_limit.R and in gh_whoami.R
```
# .token <- .token %||% gh_token(.api_url)
 .token <- .token
```

title: `.destfile` unexpectedly written even on error
description:
When `.destfile` is provided, `gh` will write to it even if the API returned an error:

```R
library(gh)

# trying to download a file from a github repo that unexpectedly doesn't exist
> gh("/repos/r-lib/gh/contents/DOES_NOT_EXIST", .destfile="gh_destfile", .accept = "application/vnd.github.v3.raw")
Error in `gh_process_response()`:
! GitHub API error (404): Not Found
✖ URL not found:
  <https://api.github.com/repos/r-lib/gh/contents/DOES_NOT_EXIST>
ℹ Read more at
  <https://docs.github.com/rest/reference/repos#get-repository-content>

> readLines(file("gh_destfile"), warn=FALSE)
[1] "{\"message\":\"Not Found\",\"documentation_url\":\"https://docs.github.com/rest/reference/repos#get-repository-content\"}
```

In the absence of `.destfile`, when the request succeeds (e.g. change `DOES_NOT_EXIST` to `README.md`), the contents of the file are printed out. When it fails there's an error message, but nothing else is printed. However when `.destfile` is given, that file is written to whether or not the request succeeded. In the error case, the JSON-encoded error is put in the file even when `.accept` specified that we were expecting to write something other than JSON.

It's a bit of a surprising behaviour, and it's the underlying cause of a bug in `usethis` (r-lib/usethis#1774). Granted, `usethis` could have been handling the error more carefully.

I think it would be less surprising if the `.destfile` were only created and written when the API request succeeded. All data from the API error already appears in the R error, so we don't lose any information.

title: Hard to work around httr2 bug re: user agent
description:
As noted in https://github.com/r-lib/httr2/issues/416, system `curl` may not have R-friendly version numbering, which is implicitly assumed in httr2 v1.0.0 (current CRAN).

That's fixed in dev but not yet released. In the meantime, I'm still hitting that error transiently from a call to `gh()`:

```
traceback()
12: stop(gettextf("invalid version specification %s", paste(sQuote(unique(x[!ok])), 
        collapse = ", ")), call. = FALSE, domain = NA)
11: .make_numeric_version(x, strict, .standard_regexps()$valid_numeric_version)
10: numeric_version(x)
9: FUN(X[[i]], ...)
8: lapply(list(...), as.numeric_version)
7: c.numeric_version(httr2 = utils::packageVersion("httr2"), `r-curl` = utils::packageVersion("curl"), 
       libcurl = curl::curl_version()$version)
6: c(httr2 = utils::packageVersion("httr2"), `r-curl` = utils::packageVersion("curl"), 
       libcurl = curl::curl_version()$version)
5: req_user_agent(req)
4: req_handle(req)
3: httr2::req_perform(req, path = x$dest)
2: gh_make_request(req)
1: gh(sprintf(issue_query_fmt, user, repo, page))
```

My debugging skills may be failing me, but AFAICT there's no easy way for me to work around this issue.

Would it be possible to expose a way to set `req_user_agent` manually in the call to `gh()`, probably through `params=`?

AIUI support is currently limited to setting these parameters manually:

https://github.com/r-lib/gh/blob/ee2dbed977d71f2a3bae6d118d6a1a597d9575d2/R/gh_request.R#L38-L43

title: Generalize gh plumbing?
description:
I'm a huge fan of how `gh` parses and builds an HTTP request. As I rely more and more on web APIs, I'm quickly desiring a layer of abstract that allows for me to just copy and paste the endpoint information from the web API. e.g.

```
GET /api/v1/quiz_submissions/:quiz_submission_id/questions
```

https://canvas.instructure.com/doc/api/quiz_submissions.html

The function would then: 1. choose the appropriate verb and 2. parse with the parameters in the string.  The present way that I'm accomplishing this is: 

```r
paste0("GET /api/v1/quiz_submissions/", quiz_submission_id,"/questions")
# or 
glue::glue("GET /api/v1/quiz_submissions/{{quiz_submission_id}}/questions")
```

Thus, to this end, would there be any objection if I worked on a package {rest} that generalized the request build held by `gh`? c.f.

https://github.com/r-lib/gh/blob/master/R/gh_request.R

title: Basic token validation
description:
Somewhat related to https://github.com/r-lib/gh/issues/133 but simpler:

I have been debugging a `GitHub API error (422): 422 Unprocessable Entity` for a long time. The problem was that the GHA UI where you have to save secrets had appended a `\n` at the end of the secret. Apparently this makes the token invalid.

It would make sense to have `gh` do some basic validation on the token format, before calling to the API. Something as simple as `grepl('[a-f0-9]{40}$',  token)` could work.

description: It seems that `gh` is able to successfully read the JSON information about a release -- including information about any assets which are attached to it -- but it cannot download the binary file (examples based on [this public repository](https://github.com/aammd/test_idea/releases): ```r # this works fine gh::gh("https://api.github.com/repos/aammd/test_idea/releases/assets/2998763") gh::gh("/repos/:owner/:repo/releases/assets/:id", owner = "aammd", repo = "test_idea", id = "2998763") # this does not gh::gh("https://api.github.com/repos/aammd/test_idea/releases/assets/2998763", .send_headers = c("Accept" = "application/octet-stream")) gh::gh("/repos/:owner/:repo/releases/assets/:id", owner = "aammd", repo = "test_idea", id = "2998763", .send_headers = c("Accept" = "application/octet-stream")) #No encoding supplied: defaulting to UTF-8. #No encoding supplied: defaulting to UTF-8. #Error in gh::gh("/repos/:owner/:repo/releases/assets/:id", owner = "aammd", : # GitHub API error (400): # #InvalidArgumentOnly one auth mechanism allowed; only the #X-Amz-Algorithm query parameter, Signature query string parameter or the Authorization header #should be specified... ``` The above was from a session where I have my `GITHUB_TOKEN` set. In this case, the problem is caused by authentification information being communicated twice: once in a header and once in the URL itself. This happens even though the repo is public (and authentification is not necessary) If I remove my `GITHUB_TOKEN`, a different problem appears: ```r Sys.setenv(GITHUB_TOKEN = "") gh::gh("https://api.github.com/repos/aammd/test_idea/releases/assets/2998763", .send_headers = c("Accept" = "application/octet-stream")) #No encoding supplied: defaulting to UTF-8. #{ # "message": "X\n" #} ``` However, `httr::GET()` works just fine: ```r httr::GET("https://api.github.com/repos/aammd/test_idea/releases/assets/2998763", .send_headers = c("Accept" = "application/octet-stream"), httr::write_disk("test.rds", overwrite = TRUE)) ``` I'm not sure where the fix ought to be made -- perhaps in `gh_make_request`? ### same problem with private repos We get a similar problem with private repos, except that in this case of course authentification _is_ necessary. I don't want to make this issue overlong, so there are two possible solutions on [this Stackoverflow question i asked](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/41696199/authentication-to-github-private-repositories-with-httr/41709121#41709121).

title: test_gh()
description:
My current understanding: there needs to be a generic tester for an endpoint. One feeds it input from an endpoint-specific element extracted from something like [`routes.json`](https://github.com/r-pkgs/gh/blob/976bc9691fdb5982aede7a9fef6cc641cd48a7dc/tests/testthat/routes/routes.json), i.e. URL, method, query or body parameters, and human-readable description (useful in expectation labels). This specifies the request.

Perhaps our augmented version of `routes.json` should include similar specification *re: the expected response*. And those two inputs are used by a function worthy of the name `test_gh()`. That gets used in a loop over endpoints, exploiting httrmock, to test the API.

Based on what's already in the few tests, these seem to be key expectations:

  * [ ] HTTP status (default: 200), e.g. `expect_s3_class(e, "http_error_401")`
    - Class is `github_response`, e.g. `expect_s3_class(res, "gh_response")`, if status <400. Or `github_error`, otherwise, in which case we must catch it.
    - This could be the bare minimum default expectation for any request in the system?
  * [ ] Specific names present in content list, e.g. `expect_true(all(c("id", "name", "full_name") %in% names(res[[1]])))`
  * [ ] Specific name-value pairs present in content list, e.g. `expect_identical(res[["login"]], "gh-testing")`, `expect_false(res$has_wiki)`
  * [ ] Specific qualities for a specific value, e.g. `expect_match(res[["scopes"]], "\\brepo\\b")`

Some of these expectations seem straightforward to auto-generate from JSON/list. Others, such as the last one using `expect_match()`, might be more trouble than they are worth. We could include an optional field for hand-written expectations and put such stuff there?

@gaborcsardi Am I on the right track? Question I already have: one test per endpoint or allow for multiple, i.e. maybe you want to hit it with more than one set of inputs?

gh_set_endpoint <- function(x) {

  if (!grepl(":", x$endpoint) || length(params) == 0L || has_no_names(params)) {
    return(x)

  params <- Filter(Negate(is.null), params)

title: Testing token management
description:
The gh package prefers the token in `GITHUB_PAT` over that in `GITHUB_TOKEN`:

``` r
gh_token <- function() {
  token <- Sys.getenv('GITHUB_PAT', "")
  if (token == "") Sys.getenv("GITHUB_TOKEN", "") else token
}
```

But the testing setup enacts the testing account's token via `GITHUB_TOKEN` (only):

``` r
if (file.exists("github-token.txt")) {
  Sys.setenv(GITHUB_TOKEN = readLines("github-token.txt", n = 1))
  ...
}
```

If a developer has no `GITHUB_PAT`, then when the tests run, the testing token is used and all is well. I suspect this is true for @gaborcsardi.

But I have `GITHUB_PAT` defined with my personal PAT, so to ensure the testing token is used I need to  call `gh()` like so:

``` r
gh(..., .token = Sys.getenv("GITHUB_TOKEN"))
```

It seems like we should do one of these things and I think the second is a better idea:

  1. In `helper.R`, set both `GITHUB_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_PAT` to the testing token.
  1. Agree to specify the testing token explicitly in `gh()` calls in the tests.

What if we agree to store the testing token in its own env var? Then we can all define it in our usual way (e.g. in `.Renviron`). We can have a helper that retrieves it. Existence of this env var becomes the condition in `helper.R` instead of the existence of `github-token.txt`. And all `gh()` calls in tests use the helper to explicitly use the testing token.

I think this might be a nicer development workflow.

`helper.R` would look more like this:

``` r
tt <- function() Sys.getenv("GH_TESTING_TOKEN", NA)

...

if (!is.na(Sys.getenv("GH_TESTING_TOKEN")) {
  ## the mocking stuff still goes here
}
```

And a `gh()` call in the typical test looks like so:

``` r
gh(..., .token = tt())
```

Side benefit: if you ever wanted to make HTTP calls from travis or appveyor, now you just need to encrypt an env var vs a file.

If you approve @gaborcsardi, I will make the PR.
